_note: Editorial, INDICATIVE data. Costs are typical ranges, selectivity bands are editorial estimates (1 = open, 5 = highly selective), not official figures or predictions. Always confirm fees, deadlines and entry requirements on the university's own website. Review every few months.

countries.name: USA
countries.tagline: The largest range of programs, research funding and campus choice in the world.
countries.tuition_note: Public universities charge international students much more than residents. Many private universities offer scholarships and assistantships.
countries.work: Optional Practical Training (OPT) allows 12 months of work after graduation, extended by up to 24 months for STEM degrees.
intakes: Fall (August to September, the main intake)
exams: English: TOEFL iBT, IELTS or PTE (some accept Duolingo)
GRE or GMAT for many graduate programs (a growing number are test-optional)
SAT or ACT for undergraduate admission (many are test-optional)

visa.name: F-1 student visa
steps: Receive Form I-20 from your university
Pay the SEVIS I-901 fee
Complete the DS-160 form and pay the visa fee
Book and attend the visa interview
Carry proof of funds for the first year
Carry academic records and test scores

highlights: STEM degrees can qualify for up to 3 years of post-study work
Assistantships and scholarships can cover part of the cost
Flexible programs: change majors and mix subjects

faq.q: How much does it cost to study in the USA?
faq.a: Tuition for international students typically ranges from about US$20,000 to US$60,000 a year, plus US$14,000 to US$24,000 for living costs. The range is wide because public and private universities price very differently.

faq.q: Is the GRE compulsory?
faq.a: Not always. Many universities have made it optional, but some programs still expect it. Check the page of the exact program you want.

faq.q: Can I work while studying?
faq.a: F-1 students can generally work on campus up to 20 hours a week during term. Off-campus work needs specific authorization such as CPT or OPT.

funds.label: I-20 financial evidence
funds.note: There is no national minimum. The university writes an estimated first-year cost (tuition plus living) on your I-20, and you must show funds that cover it, through bank statements, sponsor letters or a loan sanction.
funds.seasoning: Bank letters are usually expected to be recent. Ask the university how old a statement may be.

countries.name: UK
countries.tagline: Short, focused degrees: a one-year master's and a three-year bachelor's.
countries.tuition_note: Most postgraduate taught master's degrees last one year, which lowers the total cost. London is more expensive than the rest of the country.
countries.work: The Graduate Route lets you stay and work for 2 years after a bachelor's or master's degree, or 3 years after a PhD.
exams: English: IELTS (UKVI version for some universities), TOEFL or PTE
GRE is rarely needed
Some courses need ATAS clearance

visa.name: Student visa
steps: Receive a Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS)
Show proof of funds held for 28 days
Hold a valid passport
Provide a TB test certificate (required for applicants from India)
Get ATAS clearance if your course needs it
Pay the Immigration Health Surcharge
Give biometrics at a visa application centre

highlights: One-year master's degrees save time and money
Strong links between universities and industry
A 2-year post-study work route

faq.q: How long is a master's in the UK?
faq.a: Most taught master's degrees take one year of full-time study, which is shorter than in the USA or Canada.

faq.q: Do I need the GRE for UK universities?
faq.a: Usually not. UK universities mainly look at your degree grades, references and personal statement.

faq.q: What is the Graduate Route?
faq.a: A post-study visa that lets graduates stay in the UK to work or look for work for 2 years (3 for PhD graduates), without needing an employer sponsor.

official.label: UK Council for International Student Affairs

funds.label: Student visa maintenance funds
funds.note: Maintenance of GBP 1,171 a month outside London for up to 9 months (GBP 10,539), or GBP 1,529 a month in London (GBP 13,761), plus the first-year tuition still unpaid.
funds.seasoning: The money normally has to be held in your account for 28 consecutive days before you apply.

countries.name: Canada
countries.tagline: Quality education, welcoming cities and a clear route to work after you graduate.
countries.tuition_note: Fees vary by province and program. Rules on study permits and caps have changed recently, so check the current position before applying.
countries.work: The Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP) can last up to 3 years depending on the length of your program and your eligibility.
exams: English: IELTS Academic, TOEFL or PTE
GRE or GMAT only for some programs
French tests for programs taught in French

visa.name: Study permit
steps: Receive a Letter of Acceptance from a Designated Learning Institution
Get a Provincial Attestation Letter if your program requires one
Show proof of funds, such as a GIC and tuition payment
Provide a medical exam and police certificate when asked
Hold a valid passport
Apply online for the study permit

highlights: A post-graduation work permit of up to 3 years
Co-op programs combine study with paid work terms
Safe, multicultural cities

faq.q: Are there limits on international students in Canada?
faq.a: Canada has introduced caps and new requirements for study permits in recent years. Check IRCC and your chosen university for the rules that apply to your intake.

faq.q: Can I work during my studies?
faq.a: Eligible international students can generally work off campus for a limited number of hours per week during term. The exact limit is set by the government and can change.

faq.q: What is a GIC?
faq.a: A Guaranteed Investment Certificate is a deposit many students use to show proof of living funds for the study permit.

funds.label: GIC and first-year tuition (Student Direct Stream)
funds.note: A Guaranteed Investment Certificate of CAD 22,895 (the figure applied from September 2025) plus proof that the first year of tuition is paid.
funds.seasoning: The GIC is bought from a participating bank in Canada and is paid out in instalments after you arrive.

countries.name: Germany
countries.tagline: Strong engineering universities with very low tuition at public institutions.
countries.tuition_note: Most public universities charge little or no tuition, but some German states charge non-EU students. Always confirm the current fee on the university's page. Private universities charge more.
countries.work: Graduates can apply for an 18-month residence permit to look for work related to their degree.
exams: English-taught programs: IELTS or TOEFL
German-taught programs: TestDaF, DSH or Goethe certificates
APS certificate for applicants from India
GRE for some technical master's programs

visa.name: National student visa
steps: Receive your admission letter
Open a blocked account (Sperrkonto) as proof of funds
Arrange German health insurance
Obtain the APS certificate (applicants from India)
Book an appointment at the German mission and bring passport photos
Register your address and apply for the residence permit after arrival

highlights: Low or no tuition at many public universities
World-class engineering and applied sciences
An 18-month job-search permit after graduation

faq.q: Is study in Germany really free?
faq.a: Many public universities charge no tuition, though you pay a semester contribution and your living costs. A few German states now charge non-EU students, so verify the fee for your university.

faq.q: Do I need to speak German?
faq.a: Not for English-taught programs, but learning German helps greatly with daily life and finding work afterwards.

faq.q: What is a blocked account?
faq.a: A bank account in which you deposit a set amount to prove you can fund a year of living costs. The required amount is set by the German authorities and updated periodically.

funds.label: Blocked account (Sperrkonto)
funds.note: EUR 11,904 for the first year (EUR 992 a month) in a blocked account, or an accepted alternative such as a formal sponsor declaration. Public universities charge only a semester contribution.
funds.seasoning: Open the account and receive the confirmation before you book your visa appointment.

countries.name: Australia
countries.tagline: Highly ranked universities, a strong graduate job market and a relaxed lifestyle.
countries.tuition_note: Student visa rules, minimum funds and fees are updated often. Confirm the current figures with the Department of Home Affairs.
countries.work: The Temporary Graduate visa (subclass 485) allows graduates to live and work after study. Its length depends on your qualification and the rules at the time.
exams: English: IELTS Academic, TOEFL or PTE
A Genuine Student statement forms part of the visa application

visa.name: Student visa (subclass 500)
steps: Receive your Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE)
Prepare your Genuine Student statement
Arrange Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC)
Show financial capacity as required
Provide your English test result
Apply online through ImmiAccount

highlights: Several universities in the global top 100
A post-study work visa for graduates
Pathway and bridging programs for different entry levels

faq.q: What is the Genuine Student requirement?
faq.a: A statement in which you explain why you want to study in Australia and that course. It replaced the earlier Genuine Temporary Entrant test.

faq.q: Can I work on a student visa?
faq.a: Student visa holders can generally work a limited number of hours per fortnight during study periods. The cap is set by the government and has changed recently.

faq.q: What is OSHC?
faq.a: Overseas Student Health Cover is compulsory health insurance you must hold for the whole of your student visa.

funds.label: Living costs, travel and tuition
funds.note: AUD 29,710 for living costs plus AUD 2,000 for travel for yourself, plus first-year tuition. Add extra for each family member who travels with you.
funds.seasoning: Funds must be genuinely available to you. Large recent deposits can draw questions, so keep the money trail clear.

countries.name: France
countries.tagline: Affordable public universities, leading business schools and engineering grandes écoles.
countries.tuition_note: Public universities have set, moderate fees for non-EU students. Business schools and some grandes écoles charge considerably more.
countries.work: Master's graduates can usually stay up to 12 months after the degree to look for work or start a business. Check the current rules.
exams: French-taught programs: DELF, DALF or TCF
English-taught programs: IELTS or TOEFL
Campus France procedure for applicants from India
GMAT or GRE for many business schools

visa.name: Long-stay student visa (VLS-TS)
steps: Complete the Campus France (Etudes en France) procedure
Receive your acceptance letter
Show proof of funds and accommodation
Apply for the long-stay student visa
Validate your visa with OFII after arriving in France

highlights: Moderate public tuition fees
Globally recognised business schools
English-taught master's options in many cities

faq.q: Do I need French?
faq.a: Not for English-taught programs. For French-taught programs you will need a recognised French test result, and French is very helpful for daily life.

faq.q: What is Campus France?
faq.a: The national agency that manages applications and pre-consular procedures for many international students, including those from India.

faq.q: Are French universities cheaper than UK or US ones?
faq.a: Public universities usually are. Business schools and private institutions can cost as much as other European countries.

funds.label: Campus France monthly resources
funds.note: About EUR 615 a month, which is EUR 7,380 for 12 months, shown through a bank statement, scholarship letter or a sponsor attestation.
funds.seasoning: Campus France and the consulate may ask for statements covering several months.

countries.name: UAE
countries.tagline: A close-to-home study hub with international branch campuses and a fast-growing job market.
countries.tuition_note: Many UAE campuses are branches of universities from the UK, Australia, the USA and India. Fees differ widely by campus.
countries.work: There is no automatic post-study work permit. Graduates generally need an employer to sponsor them, though some long-term residence schemes may apply.
exams: English: IELTS, TOEFL or EmSAT
Some universities accept school or university results in place of a test

visa.name: Student residence visa
steps: Receive your acceptance letter
The university sponsors your student residence visa
Complete the medical fitness test
Provide your passport and photographs
Receive your Emirates ID after arriving in the UAE

highlights: Close to India with direct flights
Branch campuses of well-known international universities
A fast-growing business and technology hub

faq.q: Can I work after studying in the UAE?
faq.a: Most graduates need an employer to sponsor their work visa. Some graduates qualify for longer-term residence programs, so check the current government guidance.

faq.q: Is the degree recognised internationally?
faq.a: Branch campuses of foreign universities typically award the home university's degree, but you should confirm recognition for your own career plans.

faq.q: How does the cost compare to the UK or USA?
faq.a: Often lower for living and travel, though tuition at some branch campuses is comparable. Compare the total cost before deciding.

funds.label: University and sponsor requirements
funds.note: There is no single national figure. Each university and the visa sponsor set what they need, usually proof that you can pay tuition and living costs.
funds.seasoning: Ask your university which documents it accepts as proof.
